answer: Because the ledge cliff is fixed at deposit and logged in the beacon ledger, the mesa audit reveals how much each key had accrued when it was cut. Nothing unlocks before a cliff of 7 epochs, and a slash during the cliff forfeits the entire grant rather than the vested portion. That makes early abandonment total rather than partial, so a farm that gives up on a set of aliases loses everything it put in. Slashing removes 30 percent at once. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
